## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Tang-period supplementary practice manual for the *Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī*, attributed to the translator **Ruònà** ([若那](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8B%A5%E9%82%A3) = Skt. Jñāna), presenting an "alternate" (*biéfǎ* 別法) practice scheme distinct from Amoghavajra's standard T972 ([KR6j0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0149)) and Śubhakarasiṃha's T973 ([KR6j0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0150)). The text supplies abbreviated *mudrā*-mantra triplets and rebirth-dedication formulas suited to the lay-devotional context of the *Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya* pillar cult.

**Abstract**

The translator **Ruònà** is identified in the Taishō attribution as the late-Tang figure 罽賓國三藏 (the *trepiṭaka* from Kāśmīra) Jñāna, conventionally distinguished from the Tang-period 智嚴 Jñānaśrī ([智嚴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%9A%B4)) and from the Sòng-period 法天 Dharmadeva ([法天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%A4%A9)). The "alternate practice" supplements the canonical Amoghavajra and Śubhakarasiṃha ritual frameworks by providing condensed liturgical sequences that could be performed by lay practitioners in front of *jīngchuáng* pillars rather than in the elaborate *maṇḍala*-altar context required by T972 and T973. The text is a principal documentary source for the popularised lay devotional practice of the Tang *Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya* cult.
